title: The Path from Prediction to Action
outcome: Return reachable states, a permitted path, and sinks under frozen permissions.
prerequisites: The mapped chapter and its notation

input_fields.edges: Directed edge list with from,to:registered identifiers and allowed:exact boolean.

equations.label: EQV4-01
explanations: Equation (4.1) asks the most literal question available about a system: starting here, what states can it get to at all?
Take the initial states, apply the transition relation zero times, once, twice, and so on, and collect everything reachable in any number of steps.

equations.label: EQV4-02
explanations: Equation (4.2) says a permission system does not comment on a proposed action, it decides which proposals can be attempted at all.
Take every candidate action available at the state, pass the whole set through the grant rule, and keep what survives.

equations.label: EQV4-03
explanations: Equation (4.3) defines, for the declared infinite graph and independent edge-retention model, the probability that the starting vertex belongs to an infinite open cluster, and the threshold for that probability to become positive.

The first quantity is the chance that the cluster containing the starting vertex is infinite; the threshold is the infimum of edge probabilities making that chance positive, and need not itself have positive survival probability.

equations.label: EQV4-04
explanations: Equation (4.4) gives the exact threshold for one solvable graph shape, so the whole argument has a number rather than an intuition.
Divide one by the number of children each vertex has; that edge probability is where isolated pockets give way to an unbounded cluster.
